name: Oryx livery (2006)
description: Pale silver-gray all over. A big burgundy oryx head on the gray fin, facing the nose, its two long horns sweeping back to the fin's top trailing corner. 'QATAR' in large burgundy serif capitals across the forward windows, 'القطرية' in gray above the windows ahead of the wing; the oryx again on the engines; burgundy winglets on the A350s.

logos.description: The Qatar Airways oryx: a stylised Arabian oryx head in burgundy facing the nose, a pale ear and cheek line within it, two long thin horns sweeping back and up. On the fin it fills almost the whole span (drawn as the fin's areas).
The oryx, small, on the aft outboard side of each cowling.

titles.style: Large serif capitals with a long swash tail on the Q, across the forward windows.
'Al Qatariya' in a naskh-style Arabic, mid gray, above the windows ahead of the wing.

notes: Drawn from 2025 photos (A350-1000 A7-AOC from the right, 777-300ER A7-BEP and 787-8 A7-BCH from the left). Titles read 'QATAR' alone, as Wikipedia describes. The fin's gray carries faint darker-gray streaks behind the oryx, left out. The oryx's fine inner lines (eye, mane strokes) are simplified to one gray ear-and-cheek shape. Winglets burgundy on the A350s; 777s and 787s have raked tips in gray. Small Qatar flag and oneworld badge near the doors not drawn. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on A7-AOC (A350-1000, right side, side-on): 'QATAR' runs x 0.115 to 0.306 (longer than first drawn), baseline just under the windows (y -0.05), capitals to y 0.42 (they had been drawn reaching most of the way to the crown); the Arabic title x 0.406 to 0.489, above the windows (y 0.33 to 0.62). On the 777-300ER (A7-BEK) the title starts at the same place behind the forward door and is a little shorter as a share. The oryx's outlines are curves: smooth.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation (a few remembered colors, 2026-11-12). The oryx branding was unveiled in 2006 (Wikipedia, 'Livery'); before it, a white-bodied scheme with the earlier 1997 logo.
